newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope makes last public appearance before hospital.
newsitem.headline: Pope makes last public appearance before hospital.

text.p: Pope John Paul began a beatification service at the Vatican on Sunday in his final public appearance before he enters hospital later in the day to have his appendix removed.

The Pontiff, 76, was to put 16 Roman Catholics on the road to sainthood during the open-air service in St Peter's Square, including 13 fellow Poles massacred by Russian soldiers for their loyalty to Rome in 1874.
The other three are a Spanish and Polish nun and Irishman Edmund Ignatius Rice, the founder of the Christian Brothers teaching order now spread throughout the world.
The Pope was scheduled to enter Rome's Gemelli hospital early on Sunday evening ahead of his operation, which Vatican and medical sources say is likely to take place on Tuesday.

Tens of thousands of people in the square waved white handkerchiefs and applauded as the Pope, who has had a spate of health problems recently and has appeared increasingly fatigued, walked slowly out of St Peter's Basilica to start the service.

The Vatican said last month that periodic inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of "intestinal fever" which have affected the leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics since Christmas.
A number of doctors in Italy and abroad unconnected with treating the Pope have expressed scepticism about the Vatican version.
Earlier this week, the Vatican denied an Italian news agency report that the Pope may be suffering from a new tumour. The Pope had a colon tumour removed in a 1992 operation.
The Pontiff and a handful of close aides are to stay in a special, heavily-guarded suite with its own chapel and a view of the dome of St Peter's Basilica on the 10th floor of the Gemelli hospital.
His stay there will be the sixth of his papacy since 1978.

The Pope has undergone major abdominal surgery three times already, twice in 1981 after he was shot and almost killed by Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca and again in 1992 to remove the colon tumour, which doctors said was starting to turn malignant.
He also had hip replacement surgery in 1994 after breaking his right leg in a bathroom fall and dislocated his right shoulder, which needed re-setting, in 1994.
The Pope also suffers a violent trembling of his left hand, which the Vatican said in the past arose from the 1981 assassination attempt.
It has not denied recent media reports in Italy and France, and the opinion of some doctors, that the trembling may signal Parkinson's Disease or some other neurological disorder.
